newsitem.title: GERMANY: FORECAST - German banks' profit growth seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - German banks' profit growth seen slowing.

text.p: Germany's top commercial banks are set to report buoyant earnings growth for the first nine months of 1996, but the rate of increase will in most cases have slowed from the first half, analysts said on Wednesday.
The slowdown is partly due to the effect on year-on-year results of a strong performance in the second half of last year, when unexpectedly buoyant business gave bank earnings a late push, they said.

"The third quarter should have been slightly weaker, because we had a little more uncertainty on the capital markets and more volatility in stock and bond markets," said Olaf Conrad, banking analyst at Morgan Stanley.
"It could be that some banks did not earn quite as much in the third quarter."

Deutsche Bank AG, by far the largest of the top five commercial banks and the only German bank to report under International Accounting Standards (IAS), opens the earnings season on Thursday, October 24.

Analysts on average expect Deutsche to report net profit of about 1.7 billion marks ($1.11 billion), up between seven and eight percent year-on-year, marking a slowdown from 15 percent growth in the first half.
The year-on-year comparison is made difficult by the absence of year-earlier figures, since Deutsche only switched to IAS this year and has not provided comparable interim 1994 figures.

Analysts said Deutsche's earnings will suffer from added risk provisions to cover the injection of 180 million pounds ($288 million) into its British unit Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), hit by irregularities which came to light in September at three of its unit trusts.
But the impact on Deutsche's nine-month earnings is hard to assess because it is unclear how much the bank set aside in additional risk provisions during the third quarter.
Forecasts for Deutsche's operating profit after provisions average 3.62 billion marks and range from 3.58 billion to 3.68 billion. Deutsche will not hold a news conference.

Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, Germany's number four commercial bank which has been rumoured as a takeover candidate in recent months amid burgeoning merger speculation, reports its results at a news conference on Friday.

Analysts' forecasts for Vereinsbank's operating profit average 1.05 billion marks, a rise of 20 percent. Forecasts range from 990 million marks to 1.09 billion. The bank had reported a 24 percent rise at the half-year stage.

Dresdner Bank AG, the second largest commercial bank, follows on October 31. Its operating profit is expected on average to total 1.95 billion marks, up 34 percent, with forecasts ranging from 1.82 billion marks to 2.04 billion.
The bank had reported a 44 percent jump in operating profit after six months.

The year-on-year comparison will be boosted by the first-time inclusion of Dresdner's profitable British investment bank unit Kleinwort Benson which it bought last year. Kleinwort was consolidated in Dresdner's profit-and-loss account at the end of September 1995.

Commerzbank AG holds a news conference on November 5, and is expected to again outshine its rivals in terms of earnings growth with operating profit seen at 1.8 billion marks on average, a rise of 47.5 percent -- unchanged from the 47.6 percent rise reported after the first six months.
Forecasts for Commerzbank ranged from 1.71 billion marks to 1.92 billion.
Unlike Deutsche and Dresdner, Commerzbank's year-on-year comparison will benefit from a relatively weak second-half of 1995 when earnings growth slowed, analysts said.

Finally, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG publishes its results at a news conference on November 14. Its operating profit is put at 915 million marks on average, up 24.5 percent. Earnings had risen 22.2 percent in the first six months. Forecasts range from 910 million to 920 million marks.
